answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks by tying identity to locked collateral: each new key must post a stake before it can accept jobs or vote. Splitting one agent into many does not create free influence, because the attacker funds every clone and pays the same total bond, while each copy gets a smaller share of work. Slashing burns the stake if a clone double-signs or relays forged proofs. A plotted island of fake workers still shows a plume of shared funding, and a sudden comet swarm of keys costs real capital, so mass registration never beats honest staking.
